description: Native Markdown resilience plan for the fictional city of Harbor Point, exercising heading/block anchors, repeated subsection names, and a Markdown table; drafted into a six-section Green Climate Fund concept note, then verified and edited.

source.source_label: Harbor Point Heat and Stormwater Resilience Plan
source.provenance: Synthetic document written for this golden set. Every place, organisation, and figure is fictional.

facts.statement: The Harbor Point City Council adopted the plan on 14 March 2026.

evidence.text: The plan was adopted by the Harbor Point City Council on 14 March 2026.

facts.statement: Harbor Point has 182,400 residents.
Harbor Point recorded 23 days above 35 °C in 2025, against a 1991-2020 average of 9 days per year.

evidence.text: Harbor Point recorded 23 days above 35 °C in 2025, compared with an average of 9 such days per year between 1991 and 2020.

facts.statement: Street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event.

evidence.text: Street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event.

facts.statement: The plan will plant 4,800 street trees along 12 cool corridors in Eastside and Millbrook.

evidence.text: The plan will plant 4,800 street trees along 12 cool corridors connecting schools, clinics, and transit stops in Eastside and Millbrook.

facts.statement: The plan will build 85 bioretention cells and convert 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards.

evidence.text: The plan will build 85 bioretention cells and convert 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards into permeable green play areas.

facts.statement: The programme costs USD 26.5 million, of which USD 18.6 million is sought from external grants.

evidence.text: The total programme cost is USD 26.5 million. Harbor Point will contribute USD 7.9 million from its capital budget, and the plan seeks USD 18.6 million in external grant funding.

facts.statement: Cool corridors are estimated at USD 9.6 million.

evidence.text: Cool corridor planting and three years of establishment watering are estimated at USD 9.6 million.

facts.statement: The city will designate 18 community cooling centres.

evidence.text: The Office of Climate Resilience will designate 18 community cooling centres in libraries and recreation centres, with extended opening hours on days above 32 °C.

topics.statement: Extreme heat risk and its effects on the city.
Expanding tree canopy and cool corridors to reduce heat.
Green stormwater infrastructure, including bioretention and permeable surfaces.
Programme costs and sources of financing.

facts.statement: The concept note is addressed to the Green Climate Fund Simplified Approval Process.
The Office of Climate Resilience leads delivery together with the Department of Public Works.
The measures are delivered between 2027 and 2032.
Harbor Point has 182,400 residents.
Harbor Point recorded 23 days above 35 °C in 2025, against a 1991-2020 average of 9 days per year.
Street flooding affects 37 intersections during a 10-year rainfall event.
The project plants 4,800 street trees along 12 cool corridors in Eastside and Millbrook.
The project builds 85 bioretention cells and converts 3.2 hectares of asphalt schoolyards into permeable green play areas.
The tree canopy target for Eastside and Millbrook is 25 percent by 2032.
The programme costs USD 26.5 million; the city contributes USD 7.9 million from its capital budget and USD 18.6 million in external grant funding is sought, not secured.
Cool corridors cost USD 9.6 million and green stormwater infrastructure USD 14.2 million; the USD 2.7 million cooling network is funded from the city operating budget.
Public Works delivers green stormwater infrastructure, the Unified School District hosts schoolyard conversions, and Millbrook Neighbours Alliance co-designs cool corridor routes.
The Office of Climate Resilience publishes an annual progress report tracking canopy cover, flooded intersections and heat-related emergency visits.

gaps.statement: The GCF accredited entity that would submit and oversee the proposal is not supplied by any input.
The country of Harbor Point and its national designated authority are not supplied by any input.
The amount requested specifically from GCF and the financial instrument are not supplied; the plan only says USD 18.6 million in external grant funding is sought.
The number of direct and indirect beneficiaries of the measures is not supplied by any input.
Baselines and targets for flooded intersections and heat-related emergency visits are not supplied; only the 25 percent canopy target is given.
